name: Israeli settlement
scope: The policy and movement of building Israeli civilian communities in the territories occupied in 1967 (chiefly the West Bank, also the Golan Heights, formerly Gaza and Sinai), as the defining sources present it: the Labor-era Allon Plan (security settlement of the Jordan Valley and around Jerusalem), the Likud-era Drobles Plan (a widespread network of settlements to keep the West Bank permanently under Israeli control), and the ideological settlement movement of Gush Emunim (religious-nationalist settlement of the whole Land of Israel, in the Kookist line). It excludes the pre-1967 Zionist colonization of Palestine, the critics' legal and moral case against the settlements, and the wider ideologies the movement draws on (Religious Zionism, Revisionist Zionism), which have their own entries.

summary: Israeli settlement is the policy and movement of building Israeli civilian communities in territories occupied in 1967. Labor governments began it for security (the Allon Plan), Likud governments and the religious-nationalist Gush Emunim extended it across the West Bank to make Israeli control permanent, grounded in biblical and historical claims to the whole Land of Israel, while later growth was driven largely by cheap housing.
